raw_response:
I farm the way I always have: I look at what worked last year, I look at what the better fields around me did, and I do not gamble much on new tricks. I only have 3 mu, so every bag of fertilizer costs real money, but losing yield costs more than wasting a little fertilizer. Since I have well water, I will not let the wheat go dry at jointing and filling, and I will give maize water around the big growth time too. For seed, I will keep using the kinds people around me plant when I can see they fill the ear or boll well. On my land, I will keep most ground in the wheat-maize rotation, because that is my main eating-and-selling pattern, and I will leave 1 mu for cotton because cotton still brings in cash if I manage the worms and weeds in time. For wheat, I will put more base fertilizer and not be stingy with nitrogen, because thin wheat never catches up later. For maize, I will feed it after wheat stubble and push it when rain and irrigation can carry the fertilizer in. For cotton, I will not overspend, but I will give enough potash and spray more times, because if insects get ahead of me the field turns bad fast. I do things simple: enough fertilizer, enough water, spray on time, and no fancy changes unless I see them work on somebody else's field first.
